pr_body:
When an output command doesn't actually change anything in the output config the processing will still all be done and cause visible artifacts like reconfiguring inputs. To fix this save the current per-output config in the output data and on configure, if the config is the same just return without doing anything else.

Fixes #6280
pr_comments:
Hmm, is this actually enough?

I seems to me like this will break out if the output config has not changed, however this seems like it'd keep us from hitting

https://github.com/swaywm/sway/pull/6282/files#diff-66d6f9399c138857218e684475e604f3710684dd9deb896b66bf0ec2cacd149fR549

such that if an _input_ config was modified to contain a `map_to_output` directive, it would not be applied.

I thought about that but if an input config has changed it was the input command that ran, not the output one. When that happens inputs gets reconfigured by this call:

https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/12e223e7973f7d7132d95c6302328067dec732ce/sway/commands/input.c#L93-L95

I checked and setting a new `map_to_output` works fine both as an isolated `swaymsg` command as well as in the config during a reload. If a new output shows up that needs to be mapped to then that output will be configured and the input reconfigure still gets triggered.
I think we've addressed this in a different way. Please re-open if not.

issue_context.title: Significant input latency when processing output command even if no-op
issue_context.body:
- **Sway Version:** sway version 1.5.1-eca57594 (May 18 2021, branch 'HEAD')
- **Debug Log:** https://gist.githubusercontent.com/pedrocr/9aaf735494616e0dfa056df99a77a22c/raw/06ab4a9d9b56e4eb784a65734e8a0175061fe518/debug.log
- **Configuration File:** default
- **Description:**

There is something in sway that creates significant input latency when output commands run, even if they're actually no-ops. To reproduce:
 
  - Start a new sway session with the default config
  - Run in a terminal `while true; do sleep 1; swaymsg "output * dpms on"; done`
  - Move the mouse or do some typing and notice the latency spikes whenever the output command runs

I noticed this because I had the following swayidle setup:

```
exec swayidle -w before-sleep '$lock' \
  timeout 5 'if pgrep --uid $(whoami) swaylock; then swaymsg "output * dpms off"; fi'\
  resume 'swaymsg "output * dpms on"'\
```

This results in very noticeable latency when typing or moving the mouse at any moment after 5 seconds as it runs the `dpms on` command unconditionally expecting it to be a no-op. It's common to see these kinds of warnings in the logs because of this:

```
[ERROR] client bug: timer event5 trackpoint: scheduled expiry is in the past (-91ms), your system is too slow
```

And the pointer lag is very noticeable because of this.

Edit: removed the part about XWayland. Although the presence of XWayland increases the latency it was already there before that. The problem is the output command not ending up as a no-op and reconfiguring inputs instead.
comments:
Seems like the input reconfigure is happening here:

https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/12e223e7973f7d7132d95c6302328067dec732ce/sway/config/output.c#L482-L489

and it happens because nothing in the output command chain avoids no-op changes and this input reconfigure is unconditional. From the discussion around #5629 I think assuming this for the wlroots changes is fine as they will be no-ops down in the wlroots code but the sway part of the output config will still run and cause this kind of side effect.

A potential solution for this would be to keep a `struct output_config current_config;` in `struct sway_output` and bail out early from `apply_output_config()` if the new config is the same as the old one.

It may also be helpful to understand what makes `input_manager_configure_all_inputs();` slow, specifically. Running  `while true; do sleep 1; swaymsg "output * dpms on"; done`, and looking at the debug logs for a terminal, I see each reconfigure sends the same keymap, 8 times each, even though nothing has changed. This happens for every client.
```

[1180305.868] wl_keyboard@28.repeat_info(26, 599)
```

That would be one per keyboard input device, I guess.

review_comments:
Can we simplify this to the following?

- Create a new empty `dst` config
- Merge `src` into `dst`

I'm not super thrilled about having yet another list of output config fields to maintain.

An alternative approach would be to have some kind of `config_dirty` field, set to true when changing a field. But finding all spots where we update a field doesn't sound fun either.
